extracted.intended_audience: mathematics department faculty, undergraduate program evaluators, and mathematics education researchers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation criteria for undergraduate mathematics programs, courses (entry-level and transition), and extracurricular research/colloquium experiences, including design, assessment methods, and program-improvement recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement commensurate with abilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Students must be placed in courses commensurate with their abilities and mathematical background.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implements mandatory mathematics placement and advising programs; use placement to reduce mismatch in entry-level instruction and improve student outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supportive learning environment and caring instructors
rubrics_metrics.description: Students must be provided with a supportive learning environment and a caring instructor committed to undergraduate education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide adjunct lecturers dedicated to teaching, smaller sections, plentiful feedback on student work, and faculty assigned with careful teaching assignments to improve morale and student outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry-level course structure meets current student needs
rubrics_metrics.description: Entry Level courses must be structured to meet current student needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design courses (e.g., precalculus, college algebra, calculus I) to reflect student preparation and curricular goals; replace inappropriate self-study formats with taught sequences when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective outreach to local schools
rubrics_metrics.description: The future success of the program relies on an effective outreach program to local schools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain open dialogue and develop joint programs with local school districts and community colleges to improve pipelines and relevance of coursework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of technology to enhance learning
rubrics_metrics.description: Students need to be exposed to technology to enhance the learning experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduce desktop/computer tools in the classroom and technology-supported activities as part of entry-level and reform efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduce class size
rubrics_metrics.description: Reduce class size (explicit recommendation of the Entry Level Committee).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for substantially smaller freshman-level sections (example given: classes of size 35) to improve passing rates and quality of instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory math placement and advising
rubrics_metrics.description: Institute a mandatory math placement and advising program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use placement tests to form classes of more homogeneous preparation, which can improve teaching effectiveness and student performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduce/update precalculus and algebra sequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Institute a new precalculus course and replace the self-study intermediate and college algebra courses with a multi-semester taught sequence (noting upgrades such as a one-semester four-credit algebra course).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure algebra/precalculus sequences to be taught primarily in small classes with clear learning goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increase credit/contact for Calculus I
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduce a calculus I course with five credit hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust course credit/contact structure when pedagogically justified to provide adequate time for fundamentals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematics Center / centralized student support
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a Mathematics Center — an office with library materials, a full-time advisor, lockers, and computer facilities — offering academic advising, upper-division tutoring, colloquium, and career/graduate school information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Centralized services improve support for majors and aid retention and preparation; staff with an Associate Head for Undergraduate Programs can coordinate these services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broad faculty involvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Broad faculty involvement is an ingredient of a successful program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage many faculty to participate in curriculum projects, reform efforts, and mentoring, rather than concentrating responsibility narrowly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Departmental awareness and support
rubrics_metrics.description: General departmental awareness and support for undergraduate programs is necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain ongoing departmental discussion, shared goals, and policies that prioritize undergraduate education.

rubrics_metrics.name: University encouragement and support
rubrics_metrics.description: University encouragement and support for faculty and programs is essential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secure institutional resources (e.g., new faculty lines, supplementary budgets, grant support) to sustain program improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regular communication with other departments
rubrics_metrics.description: Regular communication with interested university departments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate with other academic units to align curricular needs, service teaching, and interdisciplinary opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory mathematics placement test
rubrics_metrics.description: A mandatory mathematics placement test is an ingredient for success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use placement testing to place students appropriately and reduce enrollment in unsuitable formats (e.g., eliminate excessive self-study placements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Careful teaching assignments
rubrics_metrics.description: Careful teaching assignments (matching faculty to appropriate classes) contribute to program success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign faculty to courses they are prepared and motivated to teach, and use adjunct instructors where beneficial to free regular faculty for preferred courses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Augment faculty with instructors dedicated to teaching
rubrics_metrics.description: Augmentation of regular faculty with instructors dedicated to teaching is recommended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use dedicated teaching instructors/lecturers to improve undergraduate instruction while allowing research faculty to focus on specialized courses and mentoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open dialogue with local K-12 and community colleges
rubrics_metrics.description: Open dialogue and development of joint programs with local school districts and community colleges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage partners to align expectations, outreach, and recruitment; this is linked to preparing incoming students and creating pipelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of curriculum and definition of course goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the curriculum and definition of the goals for each course.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state objectives for each course and systematically assess whether students meet them; use this to guide curriculum changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop effective GTA training
rubrics_metrics.description: Development of an effective training program for graduate teaching assistants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide structured training to ensure GTAs can teach effectively in large-enrollment or introductory courses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reward faculty contributions to undergraduate program
rubrics_metrics.description: Reward for faculty who make significant contributions to the undergraduate program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize and incentivize teaching, curriculum development, advising, and mentoring that benefit undergraduates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequate staff support
rubrics_metrics.description: Adequate staff support is necessary for program success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide administrative and advising staff to support majors, coordinate programs, and maintain services like the Mathematics Center.

rubrics_metrics.name: FOAM course goals for majors
rubrics_metrics.description: Students should be able to read and write mathematics, communicate mathematical ideas verbally, think critically, acquire fundamental ideas, construct rigorous arguments, understand general theory, and apply theory to solving problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design transition courses (e.g., FOAM) with explicit learning objectives that bridge computational first-year work and abstract upper-division material.

rubrics_metrics.name: FOAM topical content and pedagogy
rubrics_metrics.description: Include elementary symbolic logic, standard proof techniques (including induction), sets (power sets, arbitrary families), relations, equivalence relations, and functions; require many short proofs with grading and feedback and periodic oral presentations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have students read and critique others' proofs and present proofs at the board to develop writing, reading, and oral presentation skills in mathematics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Survey-based assessment of perceived course value
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess perceived value of course topics in preparation for advanced courses using surveys where students rate topics (e.g., extremely/moderately/slightly/not helpful) and compute means.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct surveys informed by student interviews and literature; code responses numerically (example EH=3, MH=2, SH=1, NH=0) and report frequency counts and means; note limitations such as absence of control group.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attitude/confidence survey measurement
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure student confidence/attitude toward mathematics with attitude surveys (e.g., SA/A/N/D/SD coded with numeric values) and analyze frequencies and means.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use validated attitude scales where possible; relate confidence measures to retention and achievement in later courses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment study reliability considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Reliable assessment studies are slow processes: samples may be small, classes vary in size, and instructor effects influence attitudes and outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect data over extended periods, be cautious interpreting small samples, and control/account for instructor and cohort variation where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of statistical modeling to investigate performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Use multiple linear regression or similar models to predict student grades (e.g., FOAM grades from first-year calculus grades) and identify subpopulations with atypical grade changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantitative models can identify students whose performance drops significantly and target them for follow-up studies or interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Senior Colloquium: talk and evaluation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Senior majors must give a 30–40 minute talk on a subject they have not studied in a class; faculty evaluate the talk on a pass/fail basis and provide immediate verbal feedback via the advisor; attendance requirement must be met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure is rare; students who fail usually give a second talk. Use faculty discussion and immediate constructive feedback; keep attendance records and require minimum participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student feedback mechanisms for Colloquium
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate the Senior Colloquium via the Mathematics Student Advisory Board (MSAB) and senior exit interviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MSAB (student-elected board) provides ongoing input; use exit interviews and student committees to gather actionable suggestions for improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardized timetable for colloquium preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: Standardize preparation timetable: pick an advisor at least four weeks before the talk and give at least one practice talk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide consistent expectations so students know milestones and get adequate mentoring; helps reduce variation due to differing faculty advising styles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honors thesis: format and evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: The honors thesis culminates in a formal paper and an oral defense; the student receives a course grade from the faculty advisor and the department determines whether the thesis merits Highest Honors, Honors, or neither.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thesis may extend over terms; revisions are typical; advisor and department assess both written and oral maturity of the work; publication is a possible indicator of high quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: SMALL research project evaluation procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of SMALL includes student-designed end-of-project questionnaires and reports, written faculty evaluations of students, and informal faculty discussions; student comments cover group structure, faculty direction, activities, program length, and logistics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use student-run evaluations to guide program changes; faculty should also discuss selection, expectations, and structure to refine the research experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: SMALL program structural guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Design SMALL as a summer research program with small faculty-led groups working on open problems; recommended changes include a 9-week duration, one convocation per week, weekly colloquia/teas, and groups of three students with one faculty supervisor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Smaller groups with a single advisor increased focus and productivity; adjust schedule for flexibility and balance between research and community activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: External indicators of program quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Use external signals such as NSF REU grant renewals and publications in refereed journals as indirect evaluation of program quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sustained external funding and publication of student research are strong evidence of program effectiveness; include these as part of assessment reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attendance incentives and pragmatic policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Use posted attendance records with modest prizes (e.g., 'Colloquium Attendance Prize') and relax overly strict attendance rules (e.g., require a certain number per semester rather than weekly) to encourage participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public, lightly gamified systems can increase responsibility; calibrate requirements to be realistic and supportive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faculty feedback timing to enhance student interaction
rubrics_metrics.description: Delay immediate private faculty evaluation briefly to allow students to interact with the speaker over refreshments before giving the verdict.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowing time for informal discussion benefits both the speaker and the faculty, improving the quality of feedback and departmental interaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor and balance advising workload
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep an eye on distribution of colloquium advising work and remind faculty annually to avoid imbalance; encourage nontenured faculty to say no if overburdened rather than impose strict limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Informal monitoring and collegial reminders help maintain equitable advising loads while respecting faculty discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program success indicators (enrollment and outcomes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Track increases in number of majors, enrollments, student degrees awarded, participation in research programs, NSF support, student publications, and numbers going on to graduate school as measures of program success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use longitudinal data (e.g., degrees per year, major counts, publication records) to evaluate broad program impact and to justify continued support.
